body: Mauricio Pochettino is expected to be appointed as the new Manchester United head coach later today. The Argentinian will leave his role with the United States to sign a two-and-a-half year contract at Old Trafford as Michael Carrick’s replacement.
Carrick and his backroom staff were dismissed on Thursday, with Pochettino expected to bring his trusted lieutenants from previous roles with him.

articles.title: NFL quarterbacks are under more pressure than ever from rushers. Why?
articles.summary: Despite all the advantages offenses have secured over the years, defenses are better at pressuring the QB than any other time in recent history. The Baltimore Ravens are preparing to start their fourth quarterback this year, Jacoby Brissett, against the beleaguered Los Angeles Chargers on Monday…
body: Jackson, Huntley and Fagnano were all injured after taking hits in games. And if it seems like quarterbacks are taking punishment more often this year, your eyes aren’t deceiving you. Through nine weeks, quarterbacks have been hit on 15.1% of their dropbacks, the most we’ve seen since 2006, when hits were first logged in official box scores.

That may be why more quarterbacks have started games through nine weeks in 2026 than in almost any other year in recent memory. This year’s 47 starters only fall behind 2019 (48 through nine weeks), 2010 (48) and 2007 (49) over the past 20 years, and the expected starts for Carson Beck, Kyle McCord and Fernando Mendoza will push the total up further.
It turns out that, despite all the advantages offenses have been given over the years, defenses are better at pressuring the quarterback than at any other time in recent NFL history.

articles.title: Kohli out for duck in triple-wicket-maiden as India hammered by NZ
articles.summary: New Zealand's Matt Henry reduced India to 0-3 by inflicting ducks on Virat Kohli, Rohit Sharma and Shreyas Iyer during a stunning first-over triple-wicket-maiden as the tourists crumpled to 89 all out in a 244-run thrashing in the fourth ODI.
body: Chasing 334 in Mount Maunganui to take an unassailable 3-0 lead in the five-match series, India's reply got off to a dreadful start when seamer Henry's first delivery squared up Rohit and induced an edge to Finn Allen in the slip cordon.
Kohli survived the next three balls, although the first whistled past his outside edge, only to then be bowled by a nip-backer that kept low from the fifth delivery of Henry's over.

The Kiwi bowler, who earned his best ODI figures of 6-27, then trapped India captain Shreyas lbw with the final ball of the over, to set India on their way to their second-heaviest ODI defeat, after the 245-run drubbing by Sri Lanka in Sharjah in October 2000.

Henry was unable to complete a hat-trick with Ishan Kishan seeing off the first delivery of the 34-year-old's second over - another nip-backer which rattled Kishan on the thigh pad, too high for a genuine lbw appeal - but he went on to bowl the same batter for 27 in the 21st over when the left-hander inside-edged onto his leg stump.

articles.summary: The Norwegian world No 1 will be among 500 competitors in the 10-round contest of 15-minute games. Magnus Carlsen makes a very rare appearance in an open tournament on 5-6 December when the Norwegian, who has topped the world rankings for 15 successive years, competes in the 10-round Super Rapid at…
body: In 2025, 267 players entered the Super Rapid. On Monday, when Carlsen’s participation was announced, the entry doubled in just 12 hours and is now close to 400. The capacity is 500 and Alex Holowczak, the Chief Arbiter, expects that figure to be reached this weekend or early next week. His advice to anyone contemplating entry is to do so as soon as possible to avoid disappointment. The link to the entry form is here.

All who enter will be able to say that they competed in the same over-the-board tournament as Carlsen, but only one player can be directly paired with him in the first round. Who will it be? The Super Rapid will follow the normal pairing system of top half against bottom half and the break between the two halves is likely to occur in the low 1800s rating range.

articles.title: The beautiful game: revived art prize gives football its creative due once more | Emma John
articles.summary: Football and the art world have long remained distant but the breadth of entries for this year’s award revivals a healthy revival. It may be the Beautiful Game, but in its early decades football was a rare subject for artists.
body: These, in any case, were exceptions. In 1953 the Football Association launched an art prize, backed by the newly formed Arts Council: the winning works included Going To The Match by LS Lowry, with its crowds flocking to Bolton Wanderers’ then home ground, Burnden Park. An exhibition of the submissions, Football and The Fine Arts, toured the country and the FA secretary, Sir Stanley Rous, said he hoped it would finally break the barrier between those two worlds.

Reader, it did not. But it did set a precedent that is being enthusiastically revived. It’s even possible that, after several decades of hurt, the world’s favourite sport may finally be getting its artistic due. There have been three iterations of the Football Art Prize in the past 20 years, and the latest arrives at the National Football Museum this month (from the Sheffield Millennium Gallery) with a breadth of entries that demonstrate how resonant the subject can be.

articles.summary: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes rejects the club's second contract offer, with his current deal due to expire at the end of the season.
body: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has rejected a second contract offer from the club.
The Portugal midfielder is out of contract at the end of the season, though the club have the option to trigger a 12-month extension until 2028.
United are keen to avoid that eventuality by extending the 32-year-old's existing deal and have been in talks with the Portuguese's representatives in recent months.
But sources have told BBC Sport that Fernandes has rejected the club's second proposal over a new deal at Old Trafford.

articles.title: England thrashed by Australia in first ODI
articles.summary: England meekly offer Australia respite from the ongoing sandpaper scandal by being bowled out for 131 in the first one-day international in Perth.
body: Hours after Pat Cummins emphatically hit back at Usman Khawaja's comments, Harry Brook's England folded as 21-year-old fast bowler Mahli Beardman emerged with a stunning 6-24 on his ODI debut.
Beardman nicked off Brook in his second over for his first international wicket. Less than two hours later, bowling accurately and at good pace, he had the best figures by an Australian on ODI debut.
His second ODI wicket was the prized scalp of Joe Root for 17 and he also dismissed Jordan Cox and Sam Curran in an opening spell of five overs that returned figures of 5-18.

Ben Duckett, Tom Banton and Root, plus Beardman's later victims Liam Dawson and Jofra Archer, fell driving in Perth – dismissals familiar from England's wretched start to last winter's Ashes series on the same ground.

articles.title: Man City are 'messier', but are they more dangerous than ever?
articles.summary: Trying to find a chink in Manchester City's armour is like looking for a needle in a haystack. If it does exist, it's barely detectable. Andree Jeglertz's impact has been profound in that sense.
body: City did not need to revolutionise the way they worked to reach this point, only the way they thought. Before Jeglertz, title talk was taboo. Under him it's mandated to such an extent it's written on the walls of their training base.

Because how does one learn the habits of a champion if the subject is not part of the everyday playbook? The Swede never considered the Women's Super League title aspirational, even in year one. How can it be at a club like Manchester City? All the tools are there.

Except of course winning silverware is not always the reserve of the club's with the best resources and most versatile talent. Nor should it be. That is what keeps football exciting. And, crucially here, what drives City's group to want to reinvent ways football matches can be won no matter the circumstance.
Pretty football. Tick. Threat from open play and set-pieces. Check. Stacks of goals from all over the pitch. Mastered. What else?
points: Trying to find a chink in Manchester City's armour is like looking for a needle in a haystack.
Andree Jeglertz's impact has been profound in that sense.
City did not need to revolutionise the way they worked to reach this point, only the way they thought.
Under him it's mandated to such an extent it's written on the walls of their training base.

articles.title: In a clash of the top two, should Chelsea be considered underdogs?
articles.summary: To consider Chelsea as underdogs in domestic competition feels alien. To a club so endowed with silverware and success over such a long period, it's like a dirty word. Something reserved for opponents, not them.
body: But reality bites hard. The Blues lost their title to league and cup double winners Manchester City last term, in a season where they also suffered their second heaviest WSL defeat ever to the eventual champions.

That statement 5-1 drubbing back in February was the most obvious illustration of the gap that had appeared between superpowers. City were everything Chelsea used to be; a team relentlessly driven by title-winning standards. Every decision deliberately constructed to give them control and assert dominance.

This is the first WSL season to feature two unbeaten teams after nine matchdays since 2020-21. The table reads that Manchester City have the edge, but a deeper dive into the data presents a more nuanced case.

Stylistically, Sonia Bompastor's side have levelled up this year, shifting her setup from a more direct approach towards structured positional dominance. That is something she always wanted but did not necessarily have the personnel to perfect.

articles.title: How Riley went from KSI's trainer to world-title dream
articles.summary: Viddal Riley - who defends his European cruiserweight title on Saturday - talks through his journey from training YouTuber KSI to nearing a world-title shot.
body: Viddal Riley had spent years learning how to fight. Then he taught a YouTuber, and that became the story.
On Saturday, the Londoner defends his European cruiserweight title against unbeaten Frenchman Seydi Coupe at Wembley Arena, with a world-title shot within reach.
Yet it was his work with social media star KSI that first brought him mainstream attention, training the YouTuber for his fights against Joe Weller and Logan Paul.
From a corner of boxing where popularity can secure a headline fight before a punch has been thrown, Riley, 29, arrived with credentials few of his new audience knew about.

articles.title: England crumble in Perth again as Australia win first ODI
articles.summary: England capitulated in Perth for the second year running as an Australia side engulfed by the 'Sandpapergate' storm cruised to a seven-wicket victory in a series-opening ODI in which debutant Mahli Beardman recorded a six-wicket haul.
body: England's raft of rash strokes in last November's first Ashes Test at Optus Stadium led to them losing that game inside two days en route to a harrowing 4-1 series defeat, and there were familiar failings on a nightmare Friday as they were skittled for 131.

Unlike the previous winter, the tourists played a proper warm-up game at another Perth venue in The WACA ahead of the ODI series, beating Western Australia by 92 runs last Saturday as 21-year-old pacer Beardman went wicketless from 10 overs.

Fast forward six days and Beardman bagged the best figures by an Australian on ODI debut - his 6-24 from 7.4 overs topping Tony Dodemaide's 5-21 versus Sri Lanka in 1988 - with his five-for on his home ground coming in 28 balls as England slumped, before Australia reached their target in 23.3 overs.

Harry Brook (1), who became Beardman's first wicket when he poked behind in the 12th over, saw his side bundled out in just 33.4 overs with Joe Root (17), playing his 200th ODI, one of a number of players to perish on the drive, the sort of shot that had got England in all sorts of bother during their Test trouncing here a year ago.

articles.title: England win Wheelchair World Cup for third time
articles.summary: England win the Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup for a record third time - beating France 50-38 in the final in Wollongong, Australia.
body: England can now paint the final rung on their dressing-room ladder gold.
On Friday in Wollongong, Australia, they became the first nation to lift the Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup on three occasions, defeating France 50-38 with a peerless display.
And just as they did four years ago, Tom Coyd's wheelchair side have delivered a triumph to offset the disappointment felt by the men's and women's teams, who both went out in the group stage.
Rob Hawkins had revealed during the tournament that England had a ladder in their team room, marking each victory by spray painting a rung gold.

articles.title: Italy 3-1 France: Esposito Double Inspires Azzurri Comeback at San Siro
articles.summary: Pio Esposito scored twice as Italy came from behind to beat France 3-1 in the UEFA Nations League, ending Les Bleus’ unbeaten run and moving level with them on points in Group A1.
body: Michael Olise gave France an early lead following a mistake from Gianluigi Donnarumma, but Pio Esposito restored parity before half-time.
Italy then took control in the second half, with Davide Frattesi putting the hosts ahead before Esposito converted a penalty to complete the comeback.
France threatened inside the opening three minutes when Bradley Barcola’s cutback from the left flank found Désiré Doué inside the box, but his effort struck the side netting.

Les Bleus’ early pressure paid off in the 10th minute when Michael Olise capitalised on a mistake from Donnarumma. The Italian goalkeeper attempted to play out from the back, but his pass was intercepted by the French winger, who calmly slotted the ball home.

body: Analyst Adam Breneman believes Underwood should be on Texas A&M’s radar amid its own quarterback issues with Marcel Reed.
“(Marcel) Reed has three games left to prove he’s still the guy. If he doesn’t, Texas A&M could have a new starting quarterback in 2027,” Breneman remarked on X.
Breneman further listed five names that head coach Mike Elko should consider if he feels Reed isn’t making enough progress, including Bryce Underwood.
“It’s either a great story or it doesn’t go well. Former number one recruit, elite physical tools,” Breneman said about Underwood.

articles.title: Who Let The Dogs Out? Giants QB Jameis Winston Drops Iconic Line In Pre-Snap Cadence
articles.summary: Even as a backup quarterback now, New York Giants quarterback Jameis Winston can find a way to bring more and more joy to the game. During his limited action on Thursday night against the Washington Commanders, Winston got some playing time in some special quarterback sneak packages on offense.
body: Even with the Commanders' defense holding their ground, Winston decided to run out his own version of "Who Let the Dogs Out" in hopes of drawing them offsides. Though the unorthodox snap-count tactic wasn't successful, it still drew plenty of laughs on the field.

The song "Who Let the Dogs Out" by the Baha Men was released in 2000 and gained notoriety after it was featured in the animated movie, "Rugrats in Paris: The Movie" that same year. It's also become a popular song in sports, and the Baha Men even did a spin-off version of the song called "Who Let The Mets Out" for the New York Mets during their World Series run in 2000.

As for his play, Winston was only on the field for two rush attempts and gained one total yard on his sneaks. But he remains one of the most fun and outgoing personalities in the league, dropping numerous press conference quotes that have gone viral.
So, even though the Giants fell 24-21, Winston still found a way to make the highlight reel.
